e-7886.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equations of a Vertical Hyperbola Given Algebraically
e-7886.problem: What are the parametric equations of the hyperbola $\dfrac{y^2}{9} - \dfrac{x^2}{25} = 1?$
e-7886.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin with Cartesian equation

$$
\frac{y^2}{a^2} - \frac{x^2}{b^2} = 1
$$

are given by

$$
x = b\tan{t}, \quad y = a\sec{t}.
$$

In our case, $a = \sqrt{9} = 3$ and $b = \sqrt{25} = 5.$ Therefore, the parametric equations are

$$
x = 5\tan{t}, \quad y = 3\sec{t}.
$$

What are the parametric equations of the hyperbola y2−x249=1?

a
x=tan⁡t,y=7sec⁡t
b
x=7tan⁡t,y=sec⁡t

x=7sec⁡t,y=tan⁡t
d
x=sec⁡t,y=7tan⁡t

x=tan⁡t,y=49sec⁡t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The parametric equations of a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin with Cartesian equation y2a2−x2b2=1 are given by x=btan⁡t,y=asec⁡t. In our case, a=1=1 and b=49=7. Therefore, the parametric equations are x=7tan⁡t,y=sec⁡t.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equations of a Vertical Hyperbola Given Algebraically
content.problem: What are the parametric equations of the hyperbola ${y}^{2}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{49}=1?$
content.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin with Cartesian equation

$$
\frac{{y}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1
$$

are given by

$$
x=b\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=a\operatorname{sec}⁡t.
$$

In our case, $a=\sqrt{1}=1$ and $b=\sqrt{49}=7.$ Therefore, the parametric equations are

$$
x=7\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=\operatorname{sec}⁡t.
$$

Question 3
?

What are the parametric equations of the hyperbola 9y2−x2=36?

a
 x=6tan⁡t,y=2sec⁡t
b
 x=2tan⁡t,y=6sec⁡t
c
 x=4tan⁡t,y=2sec⁡t
d
 x=6sec⁡t,y=4tan⁡t
e
 x=2sec⁡t,y=6tan⁡t
Submit

decision.explanation: Dividing by 36 gives y²/4−x²/36=1, so a=2 and b=6. Thus x=6 tan(t), y=2 sec(t), and substitution gives 36(sec²(t)−tan²(t))=36.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: What are the parametric equations of the hyperbola $9{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}=36?$
after.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin with Cartesian equation

$$
\frac{{y}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1
$$

are given by

$$
x=b\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=a\operatorname{sec}⁡t.
$$

First, we rewrite the equation of our hyperbola in standard form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}9{y}^{2}-{x}^{2} & =36 \\ \frac{9{y}^{2}}{36}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{36} & =\frac{36}{36} \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{4}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{36} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, in our case, $a=\sqrt{4}=2$ and $b=\sqrt{36}=6.$ Therefore, the parametric equations are

$$
x=6\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=2\operatorname{sec}⁡t.
$$

a
 x=6tan⁡t,y=2sec⁡t

EXPLANATION

The parametric equations of a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin with Cartesian equation y2a2−x2b2=1 are given by x=btan⁡t,y=asec⁡t.

First, we rewrite the equation of our hyperbola in standard form, as follows: 9y2−x2=369y236−x236=3636y24−x236=1

So, in our case, a=4=2 and b=36=6. Therefore, the parametric equations are x=6tan⁡t,y=2sec⁡t.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Equations of a Vertical Hyperbola Given Algebraically
content.problem: What are the parametric equations of the hyperbola $9{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}=36?$
content.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin with Cartesian equation

$$
\frac{{y}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1
$$

are given by

$$
x=b\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=a\operatorname{sec}⁡t.
$$

First, we rewrite the equation of our hyperbola in standard form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}9{y}^{2}-{x}^{2} & =36 \\ \frac{9{y}^{2}}{36}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{36} & =\frac{36}{36} \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{4}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{36} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, in our case, $a=\sqrt{4}=2$ and $b=\sqrt{36}=6.$ Therefore, the parametric equations are

$$
x=6\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=2\operatorname{sec}⁡t.
$$

The parametric equations of a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin with Cartesian equation

$$
\frac{{y}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1
$$

are given by

$$
x=b\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=a\operatorname{sec}⁡t.
$$

First, we rewrite the equation of our hyperbola in standard form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{y}^{2}-9{x}^{2} & =36 \\ \frac{6{y}^{2}}{36}-\frac{9{x}^{2}}{36} & =\frac{36}{36} \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{6}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{4} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, in our case, $a=\sqrt{6}$ and $b=\sqrt{4}=2.$ Therefore, the parametric equations are

$$
x=2\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=\sqrt{6}\operatorname{sec}⁡t.
$$
